To determine the number of workers needed, we must first calculate the effective capacity available for standard operations after reserving space for spikes, and then divide the total incoming requests by that effective capacity.

### Step 1: Calculate Effective Capacity per Worker

Each worker has a raw capacity of 20 requests per second. However, 25% of this capacity must be reserved for spikes. This means only 75% of the worker's capacity is available for the steady-state load.

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = \text{Raw Capacity} \times (1 - \text{Spike Reserve})
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times (1 - 0.25)
$$

$$
\text{Effective Capacity per Worker} = 20 \times 0.75 = 15 \text{ requests per second}
$$
